questions.questionText:
Which conditions cause gas particles to move the fastest and the furthest apart?
temperature pressure
Which statement describes a liquid at room temperature?

options.text: A sample of a liquid has a fixed volume and shape.
A sample of a liquid does not have a fixed volume or shape.
The particles are touching but can move by sliding over each other.
The particles spread out and fill all available space.

questions.questionText:
A compound, X, has a melting point of 71C and a boiling point of 375C.
Which statement about X is correct?

options.text: It is a liquid at 52C and a gas at 175C.
It is a liquid at 69C and a gas at 380C.
It is a liquid at 75C and a gas at 350C.
It is a liquid at 80C and a gas at 400C.

questions.questionText: What is the nucleon number of an atom?

options.text: the total number of protons and neutrons
the total number of protons and electrons

questions.questionText:
An atom has three electron shells. There are three electrons in the outer shell.
How many protons and how many neutrons are in this atom?
protons neutrons

Which row gives the number of covalent bonds in one molecule of ammonia and in
one molecule of hydrogen chloride?
ammonia hydrogen chloride

What is the definition of electrolysis?

options.text: the formation of a positive ion by the removal of electrons using an electric current
the decomposition of an ionic compound, when molten or in aqueous solution, by the passage of an electric current
the substance containing ions through which an electric current can pass
the coating of a metal with a different metal by passing an electric current through an aqueous solution of an ionic salt

options.text: Both the anode and cathode are made of carbon.
The copper spoon is the anode.
Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is the electrolyte.

questions.questionText:
J, L and M are elements in the Periodic Table.
● J has the highest density.
● L has the highest reactivity with water.
● M has the highest atomic number.
Which row identifies the elements J, L and M?
J L M
Which statement about elements in Group I of the Periodic Table is correct?

options.text: Rubidium has a greater density than caesium.
Lithium has a higher melting point than potassium.
Potassium is more reactive than rubidium.
Rubidium atoms have more outer shell electrons than sodium atoms.

questions.questionText:
The bodies of aircraft are often made using aluminium.
Which two properties of aluminium make it suitable for this use?
property 1 property 2

options.text: good conductor of electricity good conductor of heat
good conductor of heat low density

questions.questionText:
Four metals, P, Q, R and S, are added separately to water and to dilute hydrochloric acid.
The table shows the results.
observation observation with dilute
with water hydrochloric acid
P no reaction fizzes slowly
Q fizzes rapidly fizzes rapidly
R no reaction no reaction
S fizzes slowly fizzes rapidly
Which conclusion can be made from these observations?

options.text: P is the least reactive of the four metals.
Q is more reactive than S.
Q is less reactive than P.
R is the most reactive of the four metals.

questions.questionText:
Iron is extracted from its ore in the blast furnace.
Which statement about one of the reactions in the blast furnace is correct?

options.text: Carbon monoxide is reduced to carbon dioxide.
Iron(III) oxide is reduced by carbon dioxide.
Slag is produced when calcium carbonate reacts with carbon dioxide.
The reaction that heats the blast furnace produces carbon dioxide.

questions.questionText:
Fractional distillation is used to separate petroleum into its fractions.
Which statement about the fractional distillation of petroleum is correct?

options.text: The kerosene fraction is used as a fuel for ships.
The fractions with the highest boiling points are extracted from the top of the fractionating column.
The naphtha fraction contains larger hydrocarbon molecules than the lubricating oil fraction.
The refinery gas fraction contains hydrocarbon molecules which consist of five atoms.

questions.questionText:
Fertilisers are mixtures of different compounds used to increase the growth of crops.
Which pair of substances contain the three essential elements for plant growth?

Which row gives the relative molecular mass, M, of the first member of the named homologous
series?
homologous series M
Which statement describes how ethanol is manufactured from ethene?

options.text: Steam is added to ethene using an acid catalyst at 30C.
Steam is added to ethene using an acid catalyst at 300C.
Ethene is fermented using yeast at 30C.
Ethene is fermented using yeast at 300C.
